CANON: concordia-parishes-v3: one island, one company, one cure, one storm

GATEWAY.name: Gateway
GATEWAY.description: The front door: the kelp fleet, the only runway, the Strand resorts and the Mole

classCharacter.whoLivesHere: Captains and crews who were fishermen before they were harvesters; airport ground crew, controllers and security; hotel staff; retirees who came for the view.
classCharacter.whatTheyFear: Being caught on the water, the runway closing before their families are out, being forgotten in recovery because they are far from the city.
classCharacter.whatTheyWant: Evacuation seats for their own, clear communication, the fleet home safe.

keyAssets.name: The runway
keyAssets.capacity: the island's only fixed-wing link; closes at 45 mph

keyAssets.name: The kelp fleet
keyAssets.capacity: 18 boats, 12 active; the only shallow-water rescue craft

keyAssets.name: The Mole
keyAssets.capacity: breakwater fleet harbour; funnels surge

keyAssets.name: Fuel depot
keyAssets.capacity: 80,000 gallons of aviation fuel and marine diesel

keyAssets.name: The Strand resorts
keyAssets.capacity: 1,200 rooms; 2,000 hurricane-rated shelter places owned by a resort group

vulnerabilities: runway closes at 45 mph wind
the Mole funnels storm surge; vessels at the wall take damage
wind damage to the Strand roofs
cut off from the city when the Gateway-Summit road goes

sheet.produces: Raw kelp (60 tons a day to Heartland's works), tourist money, access by air
sheet.needs: Power and water from Heartland; diesel from Haven; medical care from Summit; a clear ring road west
sheet.uniquelyHolds: The runway, the fleet, the Mole, the Strand's beds
sheet.shares: Evacuation seats, boats, hotel beds, hotel generators, the terminal's 600 places
sheet.temptedToHoard: Seats for residents over tourists and other parishes' sick; boats kept safe in the Mole; the hotels' beds and generators
sheet.coreQuestion: When do you stop betting that you have more time, and whose seat do you give away when you lose the bet?

HEARTLAND.name: Heartland
HEARTLAND.description: The crater: Concordia Dam, the lake, the water, and the kelp works that make thalassarin concentrate

classCharacter.whoLivesHere: Dam operators, water specialists, high-voltage electricians, heavy-equipment crews, and the works' shift crews who commute up from Summit and Keystone.
classCharacter.whatTheyFear: Dam failure, being blamed for prioritisation, making the spillway call wrong.
classCharacter.whatTheyWant: Autonomy to make safety decisions and respect for the gauges.

keyAssets.name: Concordia Dam
keyAssets.capacity: 45 MW, eighty percent of the island's power

keyAssets.name: Crater lake and treatment plant
keyAssets.capacity: 8 million gallons a day, including Keystone's ultrapure line

keyAssets.name: The kelp works
keyAssets.capacity: thalassarin concentrate; 18-hour cycles; four days of concentrate declared

keyAssets.name: The dam's interior shelter
keyAssets.capacity: 300 places; the safest ground on the island

keyAssets.name: Maintenance complex
keyAssets.capacity: heavy equipment, 120 workers, ten large generators held as dam spares

vulnerabilities: dam stress and the spillway decision
crater roads slide and flood early
isolated inside the island from T-18h
no medical care of its own

sheet.needs: Kelp from Gateway; a crater road; diesel for the control generators; someone downstream who answers before the spillway opens
sheet.uniquelyHolds: The Priority Schedule, the spillway, the dam shelter, the heavy-equipment crews, fourteen days of food
sheet.shares: Power priority, generators, water tankers, the concentrate, spillway timing and warning
sheet.temptedToHoard: The ten dam spares, the concentrate, the dam shelter, the truth about how long a release takes
sheet.coreQuestion: When there is not enough, who gets it, and what do you owe the people downstream of your answer?

KEYSTONE.name: Keystone
KEYSTONE.description: The plant: twelve clean rooms, the only place on earth that makes Celarithin, and Southfield below it

classCharacter.whoLivesHere: Production technicians, QA chemists, maintenance engineers, and their families in the company housing on the Southfield flat.
classCharacter.whatTheyFear: Contamination, blame, the water in Block C, losing the only skilled work on the island.
classCharacter.whatTheyWant: Recognition for critical work and fair treatment of the people who make the medicine.

keyAssets.name: Twelve ISO Class 5 clean rooms
keyAssets.capacity: 24,000 doses a day on three shifts

keyAssets.name: The cold vault
keyAssets.capacity: five days of finished doses (120,000); four hours of battery

keyAssets.name: Twelve refrigerated trucks
keyAssets.capacity: the island's cold chain and its highest-floor vehicles

keyAssets.name: QA laboratory
keyAssets.capacity: every batch tested before release

keyAssets.name: Southfield
keyAssets.capacity: 800 units on the lowest ground in the parish; built to code, never drainage-tested

vulnerabilities: power failure stops the clean rooms
ultrapure water disruption
Southfield flooding on untested drainage
cut from the port when the surge creek road floods

sheet.needs: Stable power and ultrapure water; concentrate by road every eight hours; the port; its own people's families safe
sheet.uniquelyHolds: The clean rooms, the cold vault, the reefer trucks, two EMTs, a basement rated for 400
sheet.shares: Generators, reefer trucks, vault space, the EMTs, the plant basement
sheet.temptedToHoard: Generators for the clean rooms over the hospital; the batch over the crew; vault space over the blood bank; the trucks
sheet.coreQuestion: How much risk to the people making the medicine is acceptable to serve the people who need it, and who answers for them?

HAVEN.name: Haven
HAVEN.description: The port: cranes, reefers, tugs, the fuel terminal and the union hall

classCharacter.whoLivesHere: Longshoremen, crane operators, tug crews, tanker drivers who know every road, the bars and the noodle shop that feed the night shift; families here for three generations.
classCharacter.whatTheyFear: Being trapped at work while their families are in the surge zone; chemical exposure; being blamed afterward.
classCharacter.whatTheyWant: To be asked before they are spent.

keyAssets.name: The deep-water berth
keyAssets.capacity: two ships at once; the MV Kestrel Reach and the Singapore consignment

keyAssets.name: The fuel terminal
keyAssets.capacity: 500,000 gallons on the books; Tank 3's seal

keyAssets.name: Two harbour tugs and the pilot launch
keyAssets.capacity: the island's heavy-weather craft

keyAssets.name: The union hall
keyAssets.capacity: 800 shelter places, in the surge zone

keyAssets.name: The reefer yard
keyAssets.capacity: cold storage for a consignment

vulnerabilities: storm surge over the yard and the fuel terminal
cranes stand down above 85 mph
port flooding
labour stops if the crews feel unsafe

sheet.needs: Power for the cranes and reefer plugs; finished doses from Keystone; a road north for its families; a workforce that is willing
sheet.uniquelyHolds: The berth and the consignment, the fuel terminal, the tugs, the union hall
sheet.shares: Fuel, the tugs, reefer plugs and yard space, the union hall, berth time
sheet.temptedToHoard: Fuel for the port's own cranes and generators; berth time for doses over families; the tugs
sheet.coreQuestion: When the people with the power to stop everything are the ones being asked to risk the most, who decides what is safe enough?

SUMMIT.name: Summit
SUMMIT.description: The capital: Government House, the police, fire and ambulance, the schools, and Concordia General on Hospital Hill

classCharacter.whoLivesHere: Nurses, doctors, teachers, police, firefighters, shopkeepers, civil servants, and the Meridian families who chose a real town over company housing.
classCharacter.whatTheyFear: Being deprioritised because they are not essential to production; the hospital overwhelmed; the water in Riverside.
classCharacter.whatTheyWant: The hospital does not check pay stubs; neither should the island.

keyAssets.name: Concordia General
keyAssets.capacity: 120 beds, 18 ICU, one intensivist; the only surgery and emergency room

keyAssets.name: Government House and the Island Emergency Council
keyAssets.capacity: the evacuation order

keyAssets.name: Police, fire and ambulance
keyAssets.capacity: 120 officers, 2 police boats, 6 ambulances, 3 fire stations

keyAssets.name: Emergency broadcast
keyAssets.capacity: the word non-Meridian residents believe

keyAssets.name: The school shelters
keyAssets.capacity: 2,400 places

keyAssets.name: Riverside
keyAssets.capacity: 2,000 people on the spillway's floodplain; two hours to clear

vulnerabilities: Riverside on the spillway's floodplain
hospital on a generator with 48 hours of fuel
staff cannot reach Hospital Hill once roads close
road isolation of the capital

sheet.needs: Power and water from Heartland (third on the Priority Schedule); fuel from Haven; cold storage for blood; lift for ICU patients; warning before the gate opens
sheet.uniquelyHolds: The hospital, the police and ambulances, the broadcast, the evacuation order, the power to commandeer
sheet.shares: Officers and ambulances, hospital beds, shelter places, the broadcast, the order
sheet.temptedToHoard: Ambulances and police in the capital; hospital beds and generators for its own; the fuel depot; the order itself
sheet.coreQuestion: When the people who serve everyone need help themselves, who serves them, and who signs the order?

STERLING.name: Sterling
STERLING.description: Meridian BioSciences Concordia: the campus towers by the river, the executive homes on the headland, the uplink, the helipad and the crisis room

classCharacter.whoLivesHere: Executives and their families, senior scientists, strategy and communications staff, executive assistants, security and household staff, many of whom live in Riverside.
classCharacter.whatTheyFear: Losing control, a decision that kills someone, personal exposure.
classCharacter.whatTheyWant: To be seen making the hard calls well.

keyAssets.name: The uplink and radio tower
keyAssets.capacity: the only reliable external link once the cell network fails

keyAssets.name: Two helicopters
keyAssets.capacity: six seats each; fly below 40 mph and in the eye

keyAssets.name: The Hardened Operations Centre
keyAssets.capacity: 500 places; 96 hours of fuel; 21 days of food

keyAssets.name: The research campus
keyAssets.capacity: 120 scientists

keyAssets.name: Executive health clinic
keyAssets.capacity: a doctor, a pharmacy, a stabilisation suite

vulnerabilities: lower campus on the river's flood path
communications tower and uplink in 90 mph wind
decision paralysis behind filtered reports
reputational exposure

sheet.produces: Decisions and money, communications, lift, science
sheet.needs: Power and comms from Heartland (second on the Priority Schedule); the consignment to sail; unfiltered information; legitimacy
sheet.uniquelyHolds: The helicopters, the uplink, the bunker, twenty-four generators, the clinic, the internal forecast model
sheet.shares: Helicopters, generators, the bunker, the uplink and satellite phones, money, the authority to pause production
sheet.temptedToHoard: Helicopter seats for executives' families; the bunker; the twenty garage generators; the forecast; the story
sheet.coreQuestion: When you hold the most, what do you give, and whose safety do you count as ours?

power.prioritySchedule: 2019: Keystone's clean rooms and the Sterling campus first, Concordia General second, everyone else after
